q: 1. A watery scum that is formed on top of concrete due to excessive water or excessive use of trowel or float is called
explain: Laitance is the weak, milky layer of cement fines and water that rises to and accumulates on the surface of concrete, often from excess mixing water or over-troweling/floating.

q: 2. For protection from frost, concrete should be
options: Adhesion between mortar and aggregate should be perfect
explain: Frost resistance requires minimal void space for water to enter and freeze/expand — this is achieved through dense concrete, absence of cracks, and strong mortar-aggregate bond, i.e., all of the above together.

q: 3. Non-uniform compaction may cause the concrete
explain: Uneven compaction leaves some parts under-compacted, resulting in porosity, a non-homogeneous structure, and consequently reduced strength throughout the member.

q: 4. The compaction of concrete, improves
explain: Proper compaction removes air voids, increasing density, which in turn improves both the strength and durability of the hardened concrete.

q: 5. The final operation of finishing floors, is known as
explain: Trowelling is the final finishing operation performed on a concrete floor surface to achieve a smooth, dense, and polished finish.

q: 6. Expansion joints are provided if the length of concrete structures exceeds
explain: Expansion joints are typically provided in long concrete structures once the length exceeds about 45m, to accommodate thermal expansion and contraction movements.

q: 7. A joint positioned so as to separate concrete from adjacent surfaces or into individual structural elements that are not in direct physical contact, is known as
explain: An isolation joint is specifically provided to separate or isolate one concrete element/structure from an adjacent one so that they are not in direct physical contact and can move independently.

q: 8. For preparing a test-specimen, it is necessary
options: to mix cement and fine aggregate by dry hand
to mix water to the cement, fine aggregates and coarse aggregates
to oil inter surface of the mould and the base plate, before placing concrete
explain: All these steps - dry mixing of cement and fine aggregate, mixing in coarse aggregate, adding water, and oiling the mould interior - are standard necessary steps in preparing a proper concrete test specimen.

q: 9. Which type of vibrator is generally used in concrete work?
explain: The needle (internal) vibrator is the most commonly used type in general concrete work, as it can be inserted directly into the concrete mass for thorough compaction.

q: 10. An ideal ware house, is provided
options: 15cm thick concrete floor laid on a dry course of soling
explain: An ideal cement warehouse must have all these features together - waterproof walls and roof, few closed windows, and a proper concrete floor on dry soling - to protect stored cement from moisture.

q: 11. Pick up the incorrect statement from the following:
options: space between the exterior walls of a ware house and bag piles should be 30 cm
cement bags should preferably be piled on wooden planks
cement bags should be placed such that bags of one layer does not touch the bags of the adjacent layer
width and height of the pile should not exceed 3 m and 2.70 m respectively
explain: All four statements (a-d) describe correct, standard warehouse storage practices for cement bags, so 'none of the above' (i.e., all are correct) is the right answer.

q: 12. The concrete may achieve 100% strength after
explain: While 28-day strength is used as the standard design reference, concrete continues to gain strength gradually and may reach close to its full/ultimate strength after about 1 year of curing.

q: 13. The internal dimensions of a ware house are 15m x 5.6m, and the maximum height of piles is 2.70 m. The maximum number of bags to be stored in two piles, are
explain: Based on the given warehouse dimensions (15m x 5.6m) with a maximum stacking height of 2.70 m, divided into two piles, the calculated maximum storage capacity works out to 3000 bags.

q: 14. Pick up the incorrect statement from the following:
options: with passage of time, the strength of cement increases
with passage of time, the strength of cement decreases
after a period of 24 months, the strength of cement reduces to 50 %
The concrete made with storage deteriorated cement, gains strength with time
explain: Cement strength actually decreases (not increases) over prolonged storage time due to gradual absorption of atmospheric moisture and partial hydration, making statement (a) incorrect.

q: 15. To prevent segregation, the maximum height for placing concrete is
explain: As per good practice referenced in this text, concrete should not be dropped or placed from a height exceeding about 150 cm to prevent segregation.

q: 16. The process of hardening the concrete by keeping its surface moist is known as
explain: Curing is the process of maintaining adequate moisture and temperature conditions in freshly placed concrete to allow proper hydration and strength development.

q: 17. For compacting large sections of mass concrete in structures, the type of vibrator used is:
explain: Internal (needle) vibrators are best suited for compacting large volumes of mass concrete by inserting them directly into the concrete.

q: 18. Curing of pavements, floors, roofs and slabs is done by
explain: For flat horizontal surfaces such as pavements, floors, roofs, and slabs, the ponding method (retaining a layer of water on the surface using small embankments) is a common and effective curing technique.

q: 19. While compacting the concrete by mechanical vibrator, slump should not exceed
explain: For mechanically vibrated concrete, the recommended slump should not exceed about 50 mm, since higher slump/wetter mixes are meant for hand compaction.

q: 20. After 28 days concrete acquires
explain: While 28-day strength is the standard reference for design, concrete at this stage has actually already gained more than 80% of its long-term ultimate strength.

q: 21. Quality control means
options: a rational use of available resources
explain: Quality control fundamentally refers to the rational and efficient use of available resources (materials, labour, equipment) to consistently achieve the desired quality standards.

q: 22. The process of keeping concrete moist for a certain period after its finishing, is known as
explain: Curing is defined as the process of maintaining adequate moisture in concrete for a specified period after finishing, to ensure proper hydration and strength gain.

q: 23. Compaction test for concrete is done to determine
explain: The compaction factor test is specifically designed to assess the workability of concrete mixes, particularly those with low water content where the slump test is less reliable.

q: 24. No shrinkage occurs if the concrete is placed in a relative humidity of
explain: At 100% relative humidity, there is no moisture loss from the concrete to the surrounding environment, so drying shrinkage does not occur.

q: 25. Strength of concrete with passage of time
explain: As hydration of cement continues over time, the strength of properly cured concrete continues to increase with the passage of time.

q: 26. Concrete gains strength due to
options: chemical reaction of cement with sand and coarse aggregates
explain: Concrete gains its strength primarily through the chemical process of hydration of cement, where cement compounds react with water to form strength-giving hydration products.

q: 27. The importance of batching is to obtain
explain: Accurate batching ensures the correct mix proportions, which in turn governs the strength, workability, and durability of the resulting concrete — all of these depend on it.

q: 28. The process of proper and accurate measurement of concrete ingredients for uniformity of proportion, is known
explain: Batching is the specific term for the process of accurately measuring the quantities of concrete ingredients (cement, sand, aggregate, water) to ensure a uniform mix proportion.

q: 29. Weight batching is done by
explain: Weight batching of concrete ingredients can be performed using any of these weighing devices — spring dial scale, platform weighing machine, or portable weigh batchers.

q: 30. Proper batching ensures
explain: Accurate batching of concrete ingredients ensures all these desirable qualities together - economical use of materials, durability, workability, and required strength of the finished concrete.

q: 31. The measuring 50 liters of aggregate, the inner dimension of farma should be
explain: As per the standard farma box dimensions given in this text, a box of internal size 31×31×52 cm gives a volume corresponding to 50 litres.

q: 32. Batching error means inaccuracy in the quantity of
explain: Batching error refers to inaccuracy in measuring the quantities of any or all of the concrete ingredients - aggregates, cement, and water - relative to the intended mix proportions.

q: 33. The mixture which produces a steady stream of concrete as long as it is in operation is known as ........
explain: A continuous mixer is specifically designed to produce an uninterrupted, steady stream of mixed concrete for as long as it remains in operation.

q: 34. In the batching of materials, the ingredients should be measured to a tolerance (as a percentage of batch quantity) of
explain: As per standard practice, concrete batching ingredients should be measured within a tolerance of ±3% of the specified batch quantity to ensure acceptable mix accuracy.

q: 35. The process of mixing, transporting and compacting the cement concrete should not take more than.
explain: As per good practice referenced in this text, the entire process of mixing, transporting, and compacting concrete should be completed within 30 minutes to avoid loss of workability.

q: 36. The process of mixing some mortar in the mixer at the beginning of the first batch concrete mixing is called
explain: 'Buttering' refers to the practice of first mixing a small quantity of mortar in the drum before the main batch, to coat the mixer surfaces and prevent loss of cement paste from the first actual batch.

q: 37. For continuous transportation of concrete, the method used is
options: transport of concrete by wheel barrows
transport of concrete by belt conveyors
explain: Belt conveyors allow a continuous, uninterrupted flow of concrete from the mixing point to the placement location, unlike batch-type transport such as pans or wheel barrows.

q: 38. During manufacture of concrete minimum period for which mixing is done in mixer for manufactured/crushed aggregate is (IS 456:2000)
explain: As per IS 456:2000, for concrete made with manufactured (crushed) aggregate, the minimum mixing period specified in the mixer is 2 minutes, since crushed aggregates require more thorough mixing.

q: 39. For concreting of tunnel lining, the concrete is transported by
explain: Pumping is the preferred method for transporting concrete into confined spaces such as tunnel linings, where access is restricted.

q: 40. The concrete mixers are normally classified on the basis of
options: the technique of discharging the mixed concrete
explain: Concrete mixers are classified based on multiple criteria simultaneously - their discharge mechanism, batch capacity, and number of drums.

q: 41. The concrete can be lifted by pumps through a maximum vertical distance of
explain: As per the pump capability referenced in this text, concrete can typically be lifted vertically through a maximum distance of about 50 m.

q: 42. The capacity of concrete mixer is expressed in terms of
options: total volume of concrete produced per day
total volume of concrete produced in 8 hrs
total volume of concrete produced per hr
volume of concrete mix handled per batch
explain: The capacity of a concrete mixer is standardly expressed as the volume of concrete mix it can handle per batch (e.g., a 150-litre mixer, 10/7 mixer, etc.).

q: 43. The diameter of pipeline used for transportation of concrete by pumps should not exceed
explain: As given in this text, the pipeline diameter used for pumping concrete should not exceed about 30 cm.

q: 44. The objective of mixing concrete materials are the following except
options: coat the surface of all aggregate particles with cement paste
blend all the ingredients into a uniform mass
obtain concrete of uniform colour and grading
explain: Workability is a property influenced by mix proportions (especially water content), not something achieved purely through the mixing process itself, making this the exception among the true objectives of mixing.

q: 45. To prevent segregation of concrete, the concrete should not be thrown from a height of more than
explain: To avoid segregation, freshly mixed concrete should not be dropped or thrown from a height greater than about 1 m.

q: 46. Pick up the correct statement from the following:
options: The weight of ingredients of concrete mix, is taken in kilograms
water and aggregates is measured in liters
the finished concrete is measured in cubic metres
20 bags of cement make one tonne
explain: All these statements are factually correct standard conventions used in concrete work - weight in kg, water/aggregates in litres, finished concrete in cubic metres, and 20 bags of 50 kg cement equal one tonne.

q: 47. The process of consolidating concrete mix after placing it in position is termed as
explain: Compaction is the process of consolidating freshly placed concrete to expel entrapped air and achieve maximum density.

q: 48. For batching 1:3:6 concrete mix by volume, the ingredients required per bag for 50kg cement are
options: 70 liters of sand 120 liters of aggregates
70 kg of sand 140 liters of aggregates
105 liters of sand and 140 liters of aggregates
105 liters of sand and 210 liters of aggregates
explain: For a 1:3:6 mix by volume with a standard 50 kg (35-litre volume) cement bag, the proportional quantities work out to 105 litres of sand (3 x 35) and 210 litres of aggregates (6 x 35).

q: 49. For compacting large section of mass concrete in structures, the type of vibrator used is
explain: For large mass concrete sections, an internal (immersion) vibrator is used, as it can be inserted directly into the thick concrete mass for effective compaction.

q: 50. The dimension of a 35 litre of forma for measuring aggregates by volume, are
options: length 30 cm, breadth 25 cm, height 30 cm
length 39 cm, breadth 25 cm, height 32 cm
length 27 cm, breadth 27 cm, height 48 cm
length 220 cm, breadth 25 cm, height 40 cm
explain: A standard 35-litre measuring box (forma) for aggregates has dimensions of length 27 cm, breadth 27 cm, and height 48 cm, giving a volume of approximately 35,000 cm³ (35 litres).
